newsitem.title: INDIA: New Delhi blast said caused by bicycle bomb.
newsitem.headline: New Delhi blast said caused by bicycle bomb.

text.p: Indian police said on Thursday that an explosion in the capital which killed one person and injured 13 was caused by a crude bomb apparently placed on a bicycle.
The blast occurred at around 9.30 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Wednesday in a parking lot next to a cinema in New Friends Colony, an upscale suburb in south Delhi.
"It was some crude explosive, apparently brought on a cycle," senior police officer Maxwell Perreira told Reuters.
No one had claimed responsibility for the blast, which destroyed several cars and scooters, and shattered the Grandlay cinema's windows.
Perreira said the bomb may not have been placed by any well-known group with political aims.

"We don't think this was the work of any major, known group," he said. "It could be an attempt by some disgruntled element to create a sensation during the festive season," he said, referring to the Hindu festival season which was just starting.
A total of 21 people have been killed this year in three bomb blasts in the capital, including Wednesday's explosion.
Authorities stepped up checks of cars and scooters after a car bomb exploded in Delhi's bustling Lajpat Nagar marketplace in May, killing 13 and injuring 38.
Perreira said police had been able to identify the owners of all the vehicles damaged in the blast but not the owner of the bicycle. "We have a few leads," he said.
